question: When do learned subgroup corrections generalize, and does better confidence improve escalation decisions?
status: Exploratory extension on an already-inspected public-data archive; not a new confirmatory dataset
restrictions: All candidates from a task stay in one role in a fold
Score calibration never uses confirmation labels
Auditor confirmation blocks are disjoint within a fit
All methods have fixed settings, with no test-based selection
Repeated folds share tasks and training data; they are not independent replications
Cost units and mixture shifts are stipulated scenarios, not production measurements
Bootstrap confirmation intervals are approximate, not population multicalibration or exact false-discovery guarantees
Cost-threshold comparator expanded after the first exploratory run; both the original budget grid and exact validation-boundary selection are retained
